writeup: TIC 77210120 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.5344 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 4.62 percent, with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 250.3. Pixel-level difference imaging confirmed this dimming at a peak signal-to-noise of 134.5, though the centroid offset of 2.6 arcsec from the target warrants consideration. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially new finding. The machine-learning screening score of 0.40 reflects moderate confidence in its validity as a real eclipsing system, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
